evidence: Live test against running servers (2026-09-06). Created a fresh case on Side A (case_1788668300149_ffbb929a / DG-C-2026-5293) via POST /api/moderator/cases, then PATCH .../status {newStatus:'forwarded'} to trigger the real handoff code path. Confirmed via authenticated GET http://localhost:4000/api/cases?search=... that exactly ONE case was created on Side B (case-e5e87d73, source='COMMUNITY', source_reference=<Side A id>). Separately, direct-endpoint idempotency test: POSTed an identical payload to http://localhost:4000/api/integrations/community/cases twice with the same external_case_id='test-e2e-1788668237'. First call returned {action:'CREATED_NEW', case_id:'case-c7e60c35'}; second call returned {action:'UPDATED', case_id:'case-c7e60c35'} (same id, no new row). No duplicate case row was created. Mechanism: integrations.router.ts looks up `WHERE source='COMMUNITY' AND source_reference=?` before insert and does an UPDATE-in-place on a hit.

Code-read of dustguard-operations/apps/server/src/modules/closures/closures.router.ts confirms the producer side genuinely calls syncCaseToCommunity(id, {...}) synchronously after a real 4-condition-gated close (inspections complete, no open corrective actions, no tampered evidence, legal review REVIEWED) -- not a stub.

youthCreditIssuanceOnResolution.claimed: Doc/marketing copy (apps/web/src/components/landing/WorkflowSection.tsx) claims resolved cases produce 'youth credits' in an SQLite ledger.
youthCreditIssuanceOnResolution.finding: BROKEN, not just unconnected to resolution. apps/web/src/pages/YouthCreditsPage.tsx fetches GET /api/contributions and does `const contributions = Array.isArray(res) ? res : res.contributions || []`. Live call to that endpoint (apps/server/src/routes/me.routes.ts) returns `{success:true, data:{stats:{...}, milestoneMessage, timeline:[]}}`; apiRequest() unwraps to `data.data`, so `res` = `{stats, milestoneMessage, timeline}` -- there is no `res.contributions` field at all, so the mapped array is ALWAYS `[]` regardless of any case's status. Youth credits shown to a user are always 0h/0.0 credits no matter how many cases they contributed to or how many were resolved. This is a frontend/backend data-contract mismatch, unrelated to the cross-side sync itself (case.status does become 'resolved' correctly on Side A per above), but it means the credit *display* never reflects it. Not fixed: file is apps/web/src/pages/YouthCreditsPage.tsx, which is Side A UI code outside the cross-side-integration-endpoint exception in the task's edit boundary, and Side A is being actively audited/edited by another agent this session.

issuesFound: P1 (found and FIXED): apps/server/src/routes/integrations.routes.ts (the Side A consumer of Side B's resolution-sync webhook) applied whatever status arrived with no ordering/staleness guard. Live-reproduced: after resolving a case (status='resolved'), replaying an earlier-lifecycle webhook (status:'TRIAGED', simulating a delayed/out-of-order network delivery) silently reverted the case to status='forwarded' while resolved_at stayed stamped with the old resolution time -- a real, live-verified data-corruption path (a citizen would see their resolved case un-resolve itself for no visible reason).

SECURITY GAP (found and FIXED this session): docs/audit/CROSS_SIDE_CONTRACT.md claims every cross-side endpoint requires header 'x-service-key: dustguard-internal-2026'. Originally verified live and by code-read this was FALSE for both integration endpoints -- dustguard-operations' app.use('/api/integrations', integrationsRouter) had zero auth middleware, and apps/server/src/routes/integrations.routes.ts likewise had none; live calls with no header succeeded. FIXED: added a requireServiceKey middleware (checks header 'x-service-key' against process.env.INTEGRATION_SERVICE_KEY, default 'dustguard-internal-2026' for local dev only) to both integrationsRouter instances, and updated both HTTP-client callers (apps/server/src/utils/handoff.ts and dustguard-operations/apps/server/src/modules/integrations/syncService.ts) to send that header. Documented the env var in dustguard-operations/.env.example.

Confirmed FALSE/fabricated whitelist entries in docs/audit/CODEBASE_BLOAT_REPORT.md's 'intentional duplicate' table: (a) 'apps/web/src/utils/crypto.ts duplicated in dustguard-operations/.../utils/crypto.ts' -- dustguard-operations/apps/web/src/utils/crypto.ts DOES NOT EXIST at all (Side B does SHA-256 verification server-side via an API call, not client-side); (b) 'apps/server/src/utils/riskScorer.ts (Version 1 heuristic) vs dustguard-operations Version 2' -- apps/server/src/utils/riskScorer.ts DOES NOT EXIST; Side A has no risk-scoring logic of any kind (confirmed by repo-wide grep). Both entries describe files/logic that were never real.

docs/audit/CODEBASE_BLOAT_REPORT.md's whitelisted 'BeforeAfterComparison.tsx x2, kept independent for styling reasons' is directionally true but understates the duplication: the two 275-line files are functionally 100% identical (same slider/split logic, same props, same SHA-256 hash display) and differ ONLY in Tailwind color-token classes (semantic tokens on Side A vs raw slate/seal palette on Side B). Left as-is: merging would require introducing a shared web package across two currently-fully-independent SPA builds, which is a larger structural change than this session's cleanup scope, and the existing justification (avoid cross-side styling coupling) does hold for why it wasn't merged, even though the claim that it serves meaningfully different business logic per side does not.

New (previously undocumented) near-duplicate pair found: apps/web/src/context/ToastContext.tsx and dustguard-operations/apps/web/src/context/ToastContext.tsx, and apps/web/src/utils/draftStorage.ts and dustguard-operations/apps/web/src/utils/draftStorage.ts -- both pairs were added independently and concurrently by the two side-specific audit agents working in parallel this same session (git status shows both as untracked/new on both sides). ToastContext differs only in Tailwind shades (same pattern as BeforeAfterComparison). draftStorage.ts has actually diverged in behavior: Side A's loadDraft() takes an owner-scoping parameter to stop draft leakage between accounts sharing a browser and has TTL-expiry logging; Side B's version lacks both. Not merged/fixed (both files live under apps/web/src and dustguard-operations/apps/web/src, which are off-limits for this task except the one integration endpoint, and are actively being edited by other agents in this same session); reported for the product owner to reconcile once both parallel audits land.
